$comment: Five regions, and the tone each one is drawn in when there is no photograph. The tone is a design decision recorded as data rather than typed into a stylesheet, and it is the reason a country without a picture still looks like somewhere: every unresolved slot is drawn on its own region's ground, so moving from the Sahel to the Cape changes the colour of the page even before a photograph exists. All five are cut from the Afrinkong palette — deep forest, burnt sienna and muted gold — and none of them claims anything about the place beyond what its own terrain words already say.
$contract: What a tone has to survive, measured rather than asserted. An earlier version
of this comment claimed all five carried ivory type at 7:1; four of the five
did not, and the claim described a job these colours do not actually have.
The plate letters are a 17% wash of --c-bg and are aria-hidden — a printer's
proof, not text — so no contrast minimum applies to them. These are the bars
that are real:
1. >= 3.0 against --fj-dust (#DFCFB4). The tone is the 3px top rule on every
.wa-dest card, printed straight onto the sand ground of section 03. Below
3.0 the rule is ink the colour of the paper. This is what north failed.
2. wash delta > 1.30. The 17% ivory wash on the plate has to be legible as
letters, which means the tone under it has to stay dark enough to push
against them.
3. > 1.35 between any two tones in the same family, so three greens read as
three greens and not as one green misprinted three times.
4. >= 4.5 as 9px type on a 10% tint of itself. The portrait pages set the
same value as --tone and .st-cross.is-border prints its label in it, on a
ground of 90% ivory and 10% tone — so the tone is text there, and a bar
that treats it as a ground only is measuring the wrong thing. The first
re-cut of this file did exactly that, because it went looking for
--reg-tone and this use is spelt --tone. It is the tightest of the four
and it is what sets the ceiling on how light a tone may go.
That fourth bar is also why the old set was worse than it looked. Measured on
the crossings, southern was 4.24 and north 3.03 — both under AA — and nothing
caught it because /portrait/kenya.html is the only portrait the browser checks
visit and Kenya is in the east.
Two hues carry the set, because the site has two inks: forest for the wet
regions and burnt sienna for the dry ones. Within each family the steps are
spaced in both hue and lightness — evenly, 14 degrees apart across the greens
and 18 across the earths — so the difference between two regions reads as a
decision. The previous set put central and east 3 degrees apart, which read as
a printing error, and floated north up to L45 where it stopped working at all.

central.name: Central & West
central.line: Rainforest, volcanic coast, savanna, ancient kingdoms and the cultures of the Gulf of Guinea.
central.tone_note: Rainforest and volcanic ground, and the darkest of the three greens — the region with the most canopy over it gets the least light in its colour. 9.16 on dust, 10.36 as type on its own tint.

east.name: East Africa
east.line: The Rift, the great migrations, the gorilla forests, Kilimanjaro, the Nile and the Swahili coast.
east.tone_note: The Rift in open green — the lightest of the three greens, for the region with the most sky in it, and the one tone in the set with a ceiling rather than a floor. It prints as 9px type on the portrait crossings, where it measures 4.66 against a 10% tint of itself; one step lighter took it to 4.22 and under AA, which is exactly the fault the first re-cut of this file shipped.

southern.name: Southern Africa
southern.line: The Namib, the Zambezi, the Kalahari, the Cape, and wilderness you walk rather than drive.
southern.tone_note: Burnt sienna as earth rather than as ink: the desert south, taken down to a ground that holds at 6.87 on dust instead of the 3.54 it used to sit at — and 7.89 as type on the crossings, where the old #9A5A2E measured 4.24 and was under AA on every southern portrait.

north.name: North Africa
north.line: The Atlas, the Sahara, the Nile, and Mediterranean cities older than most countries.
north.tone_note: The Sahara, and still the only one of the five that is more yellow than red — 18 degrees off southern rather than the 11 that made them look like the same colour twice. The old #A87B3C measured 2.47 on dust: a rule very nearly the colour of the paper it was printed on, which is the fault this whole set was re-cut to fix.

islands.name: Islands
islands.line: Indian Ocean reef, granite and volcanic islands, and an ecology that evolved on its own.
islands.tone_note: Forest turned all the way toward the ocean — the furthest green from central, 28 degrees away, and still the only one of the five you could name blind. It sits between the other two greens by lightness so that all three stay more than 1.35 apart while east holds under its ceiling.
